title: Revit Titleblock and Sheet Setup Instruction
purpose: Provide repeatable, testable Revit actions for using governed titleblock families, project information, sheet identity, required sheet data, revision controls, and pre-issue QA without redefining upstream standards.

applies_to.scope: Production sheets and governed titleblock usage

preconditions: The project uses or is aligned to an approved Revit project template.
Approved titleblock families are available from a governed content source.
Applicable parameter definitions are available through the governed parameter source.
Applicable sheet identity, naming, revision, and issue rules have been declared by the governing standards or project requirements.

steps.name: Load and protect governed titleblock families
actions: Inspect the project titleblock families.
Identify duplicated, renamed, locally edited, outdated, or otherwise non-governed titleblock families.
Load the approved titleblock family or families from the governed content source.
Flag non-governed titleblock families for correction or removal through the project BIM governance process.
validation: Production sheets use only approved titleblock family identities.
No unapproved local titleblock variant is relied upon for production output.
failure_modes: Governed content source cannot be located.
Project template contains outdated titleblock content.

steps.name: Populate governed project information
actions: Open Project Information.
Populate project identity fields required by the titleblock from the approved project information source.
Cross-check project identifiers against the applicable governed project record before issue.
validation: Project identity values match the approved project identifiers.
Placeholder values do not remain in required project identity fields.
failure_modes: Conflicting project identifiers exist between governed project records.
A required project information field is unavailable because the template and titleblock definitions are misaligned.

steps.name: Create sheets with governed titleblocks
actions: Create each required sheet using the approved titleblock family and required size or orientation.
Do not replace the governed titleblock with a non-governed local family after sheet creation.
validation: Every production sheet has an approved titleblock family.
No production sheet uses an unapproved titleblock family.
failure_modes: A non-governed titleblock is assigned after sheet creation.
Legacy and current titleblock families are both available and the current governed identity cannot be determined.

steps.name: Apply governed sheet identity and naming
actions: Set Sheet Number using the currently governed sheet identity rule.
Set Sheet Name using the currently governed human-readable naming rule.
Store client-specific or alternate identifiers in dedicated governed fields rather than redefining the canonical sheet identity unless an approved project rule explicitly requires otherwise.
validation: Sheet numbers are unique within the governed project scope.
Sheet identity and naming conform to the applicable governed syntax and vocabularies.
Alternate identifiers do not silently replace the canonical identity.
failure_modes: Alternate or client code embedded into canonical identity without governed authorization.

steps.name: Populate required titleblock data
actions: Verify that all titleblock data fields required by the governing standard or project information requirement exist.
Populate required fields from governed project, role, date, issue, and revision sources.
Use governed role or coding conventions where the project has declared them.
validation: Every required titleblock field exists and contains a valid governed value.
No locally invented field value overrides an applicable governed code or source.
failure_modes: Required field missing from titleblock family.
Free-text value conflicts with an applicable governed project code.

steps.name: Use the Revit revision system for governed revisions
actions: Define or use the governed project revision sequence through Revit's revision system.
Apply revisions to sheets through the Revit revision mechanism.
Do not represent governed revision information through ad-hoc titleblock text.
validation: Displayed governed revision information is driven by the Revit revision system.
Revision identifiers, dates, and descriptions are consistent with the applicable governed issue record.
failure_modes: Manual revision text is used instead of governed revision data.
Multiple incompatible revision schemes are used without an approved project decision.

steps.name: Run pre-issue sheet QA
actions: Before formal issue, inspect a governed sample or the full sheet set according to the applicable QA plan.
Verify titleblock family identity, sheet identity, required titleblock data, and revision/issue information.
Where required, produce a sample export to verify output appearance.
validation: No unresolved titleblock, identity, required-data, or revision deviation remains in the checked scope.
Any accepted deviation is traceable through the governed exception process rather than silently ignored.
failure_modes: Deviation found during QA and not corrected or governed as an exception.
Titleblock standard changes mid-project without controlled migration or communication.

outputs: Production sheets use approved governed titleblock families.
Sheet identity and naming conform to the applicable governed rules.
Required titleblock data is populated from governed sources.
Governed revisions and issues are represented through the Revit revision system.
evidence: Sheet schedules containing relevant identity and titleblock fields.
Representative or full-set exported sheets where required by the QA plan.
Automation or QA logs showing titleblock compliance findings.
Traceable exception records for any approved deviation.
future_dependencies: A dedicated governed sheet/titleblock parent standard may replace source-page dependency once migrated.
A complete governed sheet-number and sheet-name syntax must be referenced rather than inferred from draft source examples.

source_candidates.treatment: Observed source fields are preserved as migration-candidate implementation context; applicability remains governed by current standards and project information requirements.

governance_notes: This L6 instruction executes upstream governance and does not create a new sheet identity standard.
Draft source examples for sheet numbering and naming are not promoted by this migration object.

provenance.migration_note: Normalized from the source L6 Revit titleblock instruction. Source-era organization labels and placeholder identifiers were not carried into canonical identity. Draft sheet-number/name examples remain unpromoted.
